content: Coartem tablets are a pharmaceutical formulation designed for oral administration, containing a fixed combination of two antimalarial active ingredients: artemether and lumefantrine. Artemether is a derivative of artemisinin, and both artemether and lumefantrine function as blood schizontocides, targeting the blood stage of the malaria parasite's life cycle. The chemical name of artemether is (3R,5aS,6R,8aS,9R,10S,12R,12aR)-10-methoxy-3,6,9-trimethyldecahydro-3,12-epoxypyrano[4,3-j]-1,2-benzodioxepine. It appears as a white, crystalline powder that is freely soluble in acetone, soluble in methanol and ethanol, but practically insoluble in water. Lumefantrine, on the other hand, has the chemical name (1RS)-2-(dibutylamino)-1-{(9Z)-2,7-dichloro-9H-fluoren-4-yl}ethanol. It is a yellow, crystalline powder that is freely soluble in N,N-dimethylformamide, chloroform, and ethyl acetate; soluble in dichloromethane; slightly soluble in ethanol and methanol; and insoluble in water. Each Coartem tablet contains 20 mg of artemether and 120 mg of lumefantrine. The inactive ingredients in the formulation include colloidal silicon dioxide, croscarmellose sodium, hypromellose, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and polysorbate 80.
